replace.align_plan:
Answer, from inverse kinematics alone, which standoff poses facing one target from one named side an arm can actually hold.
Use when: you have a current target_ref and need an IK-only comparison of standoff poses from a named side. This is optional diagnosis, not a prerequisite for every approach. Near miss: this is not grasp_plan (where on this object do the fingers close); use grasp_plan for contact geometry and candidate finger poses; use move_pose when you already have the pose to command. An unreachable result describes this solver attempt, not an impossible approach side. If you later call grasp_plan, inspect its candidates independently: grasp_plan takes no approach_side or align candidate input, so it does not inherit this side selection. The five sides are world-frame directions toward the object and never toward an arm: top stands off above the target and travels down (world -Z), front stands off at -X travelling +X, back at +X travelling -X, left at +Y travelling -Y, and right at -Y travelling +Y. Choose the arm separately in arm; approach_side "left" does not mean the left arm. Two bounded numbers shape the request: standoff_m is the distance in metres from the target's visible-surface centroid to the candidate link6 position (default 0.10 m, permitted 0.02-0.30 m), and max_candidates is how many jaw rolls to sweep at that one position (default 3, at most 6).
Effect: read-only. No action is submitted, no world state changes, no artifact is written, and no observation is produced or consumed. Every candidate is solved by inverse kinematics from this arm's current measured joint configuration against its joint limits, so motion_planner_called is false in every result and the same request can answer differently after the arm has moved.
Returns: schema, the echoed target_ref, approach_side and requested_arm, motion_planner_called, and candidates. Each candidate carries source_index (which synthesised pose it came from, counting from 0), arm, align_pose = {position_m [x,y,z] in metres, orientation_xyzw [x,y,z,w] normalized} as a world-frame public link6 pose, reachable, position_error_m in metres and orientation_error_rad in radians at the best joint configuration the solver found, iterations (1 on this backend: one SDK IK solve per pose), rejection_reason (null when reachable; otherwise ik_failed when the SDK IK found no joint solution, ik_branch_jump when every valid solution needs a raw joint move larger than pi rad from the current configuration -- another arm branch the joint interpolation would sweep through -- or fk_residual_exceeded when a solution misses the pose by more than the SDK solver's own position or orientation tolerance) and claim_boundary. All candidates share one standoff position and differ only by jaw roll about the approach axis. arm "both" returns one candidate per arm per pose, keyed by (arm, source_index). Unreachable candidates are returned rather than dropped, so a ruled-out side can be cited. Read position_error_m and orientation_error_rad rather than trusting the word reachable, then command a chosen align_pose through move_pose: under targets.<selected_arm>, set position_mode=absolute and orientation_mode=absolute_quaternion and copy position_m and orientation_xyzw. Select interaction by physical intent. Schema example only; replace this illustrative pose and arm with your chosen current result:
{"tool":"move_pose","arguments":{"targets":{"right":{"position_mode":"absolute","position_m":[0.1,0.0,0.9],"orientation_mode":"absolute_quaternion","orientation_xyzw":[0.0,0.0,0.0,1.0],"interaction":"precision"}}}}
 There is no later receipt and no reference to resolve, because nothing was submitted.
Does not: prove that a collision-free path exists, plan or execute any motion, avoid the table, the target or anything else in the scene, or promise that move_pose to a returned pose will arrive. A returned pose has not been tried: reachable means only that this model of this arm admits a joint configuration holding that pose. It is not a grasp, not a contact, not retention and not task success, and it makes no claim about the gripper, which is neither commanded nor read. The standoff is measured from the visible-surface centroid of the segmented mask, not from the object's true centre, so an occluded or one-sided view biases every candidate toward the camera. An unreachable verdict describes this arm from its present configuration; it is not proof that the approach is impossible. Use position_error_m and orientation_error_rad to interpret this attempt; do not turn them into a probability of path feasibility. Only the motion tool attempts the actual route. On this backend this tool and the motion tools use the same SDK inverse-kinematics solve: up to 32 seeds from the current joints (the SDK's configured count, capped at 32), this arm's own self-collision checked at the endpoint, and the straight joint interpolation screened for self-collision and against the other arm at its measured joints. It does not model objects on the table, the tabletop surface, finger links or a held payload. A pose reported reachable can still be refused by a motion that starts from a different measured configuration.
On error: Refused: standoff_m outside 0.02-0.30 m or max_candidates outside 1 to 6; an approach_side or arm outside this tool's enums; a target_ref unknown in this round (target_ref_unavailable) or bound to an earlier observation (stale_observation); a target whose mask or depth cannot locate a centroid (target_geometry_unavailable). invalid_arguments naming standoff_m means the value left 0.02-0.30 m -- resubmit inside that range instead of retrying the same number. invalid_arguments naming approach_side means the string is not one of the five declared directions; re-read this tool's approach_side enum and select one of its values rather than inventing a synonym. invalid_arguments naming arm means the name is not an arm of this embodiment; this tool's arm enum is the complete list of what it has. target_ref_unavailable means no such segmented target exists and stale_observation means the reference predates the current observation: re-run vision_segment or vision_ground on the current view and use the new reference. target_geometry_unavailable is retryable and means the mask or its depth is too poor to locate a centroid, so obtain a clearer current view of that target first. ik_branch_jump is not a joint limit: the pose is holdable only from another arm configuration, so prefer another jaw roll or side, or move the arm with recover_pose or a free-space move_pose toward that side and ask again. When candidates are unreachable, use their residuals and current geometry to choose a different side, standoff or arm if that answers a specific uncertainty. Do not exhaustively sweep unchanged requests. A world move changes the starting configuration and invalidates target references; obtain a fresh target before another query. Fixed texts stated once here and left out of results and effects: candidates[].claim_boundary is "SDK IK and FK only; no physics, collision-free path, contact or task-success claim".
replace.check_task: Query the environment-owned official RoboDojo Boolean verdict at the current valid state boundary. Use when: fresh physical evidence suggests the requested arrangement may be complete, and always before finish_episode(outcome=success); a planner success, closed gripper or visually plausible placement is not a substitute. Effect: read-only call to the trusted RoboDojo checker and no world advance. Returns: task_success Boolean when available, or an explicit retryable unavailable result. Does not: explain the predicate, expose numerical tolerances, actor handles, target coordinates, task source or expert trajectory, change the world, or validate infrastructure quality. On error: Refused: any argument (invalid_arguments). Wait for a valid state boundary and retry; never infer official success from action submission or visual appearance alone.
replace.compute:
Calculate derived quantities from numbers already available to you.
Use when: before using a newly calculated number to choose or parameterize an action, call compute. This includes a single offset, distance, angle, unit conversion, quaternion calculation or residual check. Send the expression before using its answer; do not substitute mental arithmetic. Batch related calculations when useful. No call is needed to copy an already returned valid value, reuse a result whose inputs and assumptions are unchanged, or choose a constant that requires no calculation. For image, depth or calibration queries, use geometry_query; use mark_point when a current pixel measurement needs a persistent name or cross-view check.
Selection examples: deriving a new world target by adding an offset to a measured point -> compute, then use the returned point. Locating a known world target in a camera image -> geometry_query(world_points_m=...). Copying a valid planner pose unchanged -> the selected motion or execution tool, with no redundant calculation.
Ready to use: np, Rotation, math, geom, pi, float and int are prebound; do not write import statements or function definitions. bindings is a list of {name,value,from?}; numeric lists become arrays automatically, so b-a works directly. Each call starts fresh: pass every input again. Use Rotation.from_quat(q).as_matrix(), Rotation.from_euler('xyz', angles, degrees=True).as_quat(), np.linalg.norm(v), np.clip(x,-1,1), and math.radians(degrees) directly. Quaternions are [x,y,z,w].
Geometry helpers: geom.unit(v) normalizes a nonzero 3-vector; geom.angle_deg(a,b) returns the unsigned angle in [0,180] degrees without hand-written normalization or acos; geom.rotate(q,v) rotates a 3-vector by q; geom.transform_point(t,q,p) returns t + rotated p. The translation and rotated point must share the declared destination frame and units. Helpers use only your inputs; they do not choose the correct frame or robot axis. unit and angle reject zero directions and use scaled normalization to avoid overflow/underflow.
Call format examples (replace these illustrative numbers with your inputs):
{"bindings":[{"name":"a","value":[0.1,0.2,0.3]},{"name":"b","value":[0.4,0.6,0.3]}],"expressions":"distance_m = np.linalg.norm(b - a)","outputs":["distance_m"]}
{"bindings":[{"name":"p","value":[0.1,0.2,0.3]},{"name":"q","value":[0.0,0.0,0.0,1.0]}],"expressions":"axis = geom.rotate(q, [1, 0, 0])\npoint = p + 0.03 * axis\nangle = geom.angle_deg(axis, [0, 0, 1])","outputs":["point","angle"]}
The first example returns distance_m=0.5; the second returns point=[0.13,0.2,0.3] and angle=90. expressions is one JSON string; encode line breaks as \n, with no Markdown fences, imports, print or return statement. A final bare expression is available as result.
Effect: read-only pure calculation, no robot decision, scene read, image, files, network or persistent state.
Returns: outputs entries with name, value and kind. Set outputs to the final variable names you need (or result for the last expression); temporary arrays are then not serialized or counted as returned measurements. Omit outputs for the historical automatic numeric-variable results. Unreturned working values are named in intermediates_not_returned. Numbers are rounded to nine decimal places.
Does not: measure the world, detect stale inputs, prove reachability, contact, retention or task success. A computed value remains conditional on your measurements, units and assumptions. Only the listed numeric namespace is available; module loading and general Python are unavailable.
On error: Refused: a block beyond the Limits below; a construct outside the evaluator grammar; an unknown, reserved or underscore-prefixed name; a string literal longer than 32 characters; a binding whose from is blank or longer than 120 characters; an output name the block never assigned; a non-finite result, or no numeric result at all. Each refusal is invalid_arguments; read its field, received and constraints, then change that input. Syntax error: use valid numeric Python; separate statements with actual decoded newlines or semicolons. Do not leave literal backslash-n characters between statements after JSON decoding. Repair and retry the calculation rather than supplying a mental substitute. Imports: remove the import and use the prebound name. Unknown name: pass it in bindings or use a listed helper; variables do not survive calls. Output count/size: select only the small final results with outputs, return a slice/summary, or split independent calculations. Non-finite result: check zero division, scale and units; use geom.unit/angle_deg for directions. Limits: 4096 UTF-8 source bytes, 24 statements, 16 bindings, at most 12 selected outputs and 64 elements per returned value in at most 2 dimensions, ** literal exponent magnitude <=8. No loops, comprehensions, definitions or arbitrary imports. Memory/time exhaustion calls for a smaller calculation, not the identical retry.
replace.geometry_query:
Compute metric geometry from one policy-visible camera's published RGB-D and calibration: project world points to pixels, back-project pixels to world points, or summarise the valid depth of a rectangle.
Use when: a geometric quantity must be derived from calibration rather than estimated from the picture. The clearest case is world_points_m, which is the only way to ask where a world coordinate you already hold falls in an image -- for locating the commanded link6 target, a planned waypoint or a proposal's pregrasp point in the view you are looking at, and for reading whether it is in front of the camera and inside the frame. region answers "how deep is this patch" over a rectangle without naming a pixel. Near miss against mark_point: if you want a pixel measured, kept under a name and re-checked against a complementary view, call mark_point -- it verifies a repeated name across views (a disagreement beyond 25 mm fails that entry), reports depth-support counts and draws the overlay. This tool's points is the same back-projection without the mark, the name, the cross-view check or the image; prefer it when you want the number now and nothing retained, or when the pixel belongs to a saved step rather than the current observation.
Effect: read-only. It does not move the robot, change the scene, consume a robot decision, return any image, or persist a mark or reference; it reads the already-published observation artifacts and their calibration and returns numbers. Every result names the step and the source state it was computed from, and world_points_m additionally names the calibration hash it used.
Returns: exactly one of world_points, points or region_result, alongside step, source_state_sha256 and camera. world_points gives, per requested point, its camera-frame coordinates, in_front, in_frame, and -- when it is in front of the camera -- exact and rounded pixel_uv plus the scene depth already at that pixel and the residual between the two. points gives, per requested pixel, valid plus the median depth, the supporting sample count and world_xyz_m when depth was usable. region_result gives the rectangle, its valid sample count and fraction, and min/median/max depth when any sample was valid.
Does not: identify or segment an object, decide visibility or occlusion, or prove reachability, collision clearance, contact, retention or task success. A positive depth_residual_m means the scene surface at that pixel is nearer than your point, which is evidence of occlusion and not a verdict on it; in_frame is image bounds, not line of sight. A single-view depth reading measures a visible surface, never an object centre or its hidden extent, and no returned number is simulator ground truth.
On error: Refused: none or two of points, region and world_points_m, with a message naming all three; a camera outside the fixed list; a step that names no saved observation (invalid_arguments, naming the saved range); more than sixteen points or world points, or a non-finite world coordinate; window_px outside 0 to 15; a pixel outside the image, which refuses the whole call rather than its entry; a rectangle that leaves the image or does not have x0<x1 and y0<y1. Use the named view's own top-left OpenCV pixel frame, keep every pixel and the whole rectangle inside that image, and order the rectangle [x0,y0,x1,y1] with x0<x1 and y0<y1. Missing or invalid depth is reported, never inferred, and does not fail the call: a points entry returns valid false with no depth or world_xyz_m, region_result reports valid_count 0 with no depth_m, and a projected world point carries null scene_depth_m and depth_residual_m. To obtain a reading, move the pixel farther inside the intended surface, widen window_px, or read a complementary view. The camera list is fixed: head, left_wrist, right_wrist. The left_wrist and right_wrist cameras move with their arms, so their calibration is valid only at the pose they were captured at -- after any motion, query the fresh observation instead of reusing an earlier pixel from it. Adjacent calculation: use compute for arithmetic on already supplied world-frame numbers. Keep projection, back-projection and depth sampling here so they bind the selected observation and calibration.
replace.grasp_execute:
Execute your selected grasp through open, pregrasp, approach, close, lift and verify.
Use when: grasp_plan returned candidates on the current observation and you selected one, the gripper may open at its current position, and a short upward probe is appropriate. Use manual motion for articulation or a grasp that must not lift.
Effect: opens the gripper first, which releases anything currently held; a nearly closed gripper is not proof it is empty. Moves to the candidate's pregrasp pose, follows its approach to the contact pose, closes, then requests 3 cm world-up at the same orientation. The Supervisor drives five stage actions as one robot decision with no intermediate Agent turn. Pose stages use the same semantic motion route as manual move_pose: free-space pregrasp, contact approach, and precision lift. Opening uses the embodiment's open directive, not the candidate's predicted aperture. Targets are committed once.
Returns: the submitted sequence and cost immediately; on the next turn, stage statuses, the post-close baseline images and current post-lift images, the measured link6 lift (this backend publishes no jaw separation: ARX finger readings are normalized encoder values, and the close stage's gripper_outcome and the verify stage's jaw_hold are the jaw evidence), plus rigid-versus-stationary depth support for the selected visible surface. Occluded, unavailable or ambiguous surface evidence is unknown.
Does not: change candidate, retry, stop for a decision halfway, infer an empty gripper before opening, or certify attachment, stable transport or task success. Depth support does not re-identify an object; a completed sequence only records execution.
On error: Refused: a candidate from an earlier observation (stale_candidate_observation) or not published by grasp_plan (candidate_unavailable); a pregrasp or contact pose that is missing, non-finite or more than 0.001 from a unit quaternion, a pregrasp whose orientation differs from the contact orientation or that does not stand off from it, or a pregrasp, contact or 3 cm lift pose outside the action workspace (candidate_geometry_unavailable); either probed pose unreachable, or the two reachable only under different equivalents (grasp_pregrasp_unreachable); another committed sequence in flight (skill_sequence_active); the episode's terminal boundary (episode_terminal). Stale candidates require grasp_plan on the current observation. A stage that does not arrive ends the sequence before later stages, with a fresh observation; inspect it and re-plan. If lift did not complete, the final scene may differ from the post-close baseline. Before opening or committing, runs one read-only backend probe of the selected pregrasp and contact poses, each from the current measured joints, for the compiled orientation and its 180-degree jaw flip. When the compiled poses are not both admitted but the flipped ones are, the flip is committed and reported as pose_selection adopted_equivalent. A refusal submits no action and reports grasp_pregrasp_unreachable with a bounded planning summary; select another candidate or reposition. Passing covers only these current-state poses under the backend's published collision coverage. The Supervisor revalidates execution after opening; contact, lift and retention remain unchecked by the probe. The acknowledgement and final receipt include precommit_motion_check (one query, zero robot decisions). Its close stage uses the same jaw rule as set_gripper: a close that stops on the object ends 3 native actions after the jaws stop, the close stage reports status executed with reason gripper_stalled_before_target and a gripper_outcome measurement per closing arm, and the committed sequence continues to lift and verification; a stall is not a verified grasp. On this backend a refused probe's summary also carries ik_candidate_counts (SDK IK solutions returned, valid endpoints, and those within the joint-jump limit), ik_outcome_counts such as no_valid_endpoint, and constraint_rejection_counts per filter; they describe one bounded SDK IK solve, not proof that the pregrasp is unreachable. On this backend each dispatched stage action is one robot command that reserves up to 20 native actions from the task's native-action allowance, so a complete sequence can consume up to 100. With no calibrated jaw aperture here, closure_strength stays unavailable and the verify stage adds jaw_hold: likely (jaws still held apart at the close opening after the lift), unlikely (the close never left the open position, or the jaws closed to the floor or to the held drive target) or unknown (also when a reading it compares has the finger pair shifted more than 4 mm to one side), with the normalized readings, finger offsets and tolerance in verification.jaw_hold.evidence. It is not a grasp, contact or retention verdict. Fixed texts stated once here and left out of results and effects: the result's claim_boundary is "one committed sequence of trusted executions and the public measurements taken after it; motion arrival and jaw separation beside visible extents are evidence, not grasp, placement, retention or official task success"; precommit_motion_check.claim_boundary (also in a grasp_pregrasp_unreachable refusal) is "Current-state planning/admission for the probed stages, with the selected backend's collision coverage. Does not certify contact, lift, retention or task success; execution revalidates after opening."; last_action_effect.detail.verification.claim_boundary is "jaw separation beside visible extents is evidence, not a holding verdict; no value of this pair establishes contact or retention"; last_action_effect.detail.verification.lift_probe.claim_boundary is "short_lift_evidence_only;not_attachment_or_stable_transport_or_task_success"; last_action_effect.detail.verification.jaw_hold.claim_boundary is "normalized jaw-encoder readings under the backend drive limiter; not a calibrated aperture, contact, attachment, retention or task-success verdict".
replace.grasp_plan:
Generate inspectable public RGB-D grasp candidates for one current target.
Use when: current grounding or segmentation identifies the intended object and you need parallel-jaw poses. Select the arm on dual-arm embodiments.
Effect: read-only; queries Contact-GraspNet using the selected source-camera RGB-D and compiles poses to the ARX X5 link6 controlled point; the embodiment card gives its fixed offset to the jaw contact centre. Top-down candidates from the target mask (jaw centre at a support-aware mid-height) join the learned ones. Optional synchronized views provide review evidence.
Returns: up to three candidates, complete world-frame pregrasp_pose and contact_pose, copyable bounded contact_approach targets, predicted opening, compiler checks and labeled review images. gripper_opening_m is the learned width prediction or, top-down, the mask width plus clearance, admitted up to the 80 mm nominal ceiling; aperture_calibration states that it is not measured pad clearance. Reachability here is the planning-time IK reference described under IK selection below; no plan_ref is returned. Inspect every candidate panel and choose target identity and geometry independently of rank. After choosing a current candidate, use grasp_execute(candidate_id, rationale) when you accept its committed open/pregrasp/approach/close/lift/verify sequence without intermediate decisions. Choose manual move_pose plus set_gripper when you need a separate observation or decision before closing. Choose this path before moving: any world action stales the candidate, so call grasp_plan again before later using grasp_execute. Pose handoff: when manually commanding a returned world pose, set position_mode=absolute and orientation_mode=absolute_quaternion, then copy position_m and orientation_xyzw unchanged. Put these fields under targets.<selected_arm>. Choose interaction by the intended physical contact. Schema example only; replace the illustrative pose and arm with your selected current result:
{"tool":"move_pose","arguments":{"targets":{"right":{"position_mode":"absolute","position_m":[0.1,0.0,0.9],"orientation_mode":"absolute_quaternion","orientation_xyzw":[0.0,0.0,0.0,1.0],"interaction":"precision"}}}}
Does not: plan trajectories, certify reachability, move the robot, command a gripper, use object ground truth, certify retention or report task success. Backend rank is not a success probability. Missing optional review cameras do not invalidate usable primary input.
On error: Refused: a target_ref unknown in this round (target_ref_unavailable) or bound to an earlier observation (stale_observation); max_candidates outside 1 to 3; an arm outside this tool's enum; unusable primary RGB-D or a transient backend failure (grasp_proposal_failed); a request the grasp-proposal service rejects (invalid_arguments, with the service's detail). Not refused but moved to diagnostics.rejected: a candidate whose predicted opening exceeds the nominal ceiling above, or whose controlled point or pregrasp lies outside the action workspace; with none left the result is status no_candidate. Obtain a better current view or select another target or candidate. Recompute after the target or observation changes. After a submitted motion fails, use its phase and measured residual to choose the next action. Retention evidence remains advisory. Prepared grasp selection: grasp_execute opens first and releases anything held, then uses the candidate pregrasp and contact poses and a 3 cm world-up probe. Select it only when opening and lifting are appropriate; otherwise use manual motion. Candidates are geometry proposals, not reachability certificates. For grasp_execute, the selected pregrasp and contact poses receive one backend check before opening. Manual pose submissions use normal backend admission. IK selection: before the max_candidates display cap, every compiled candidate in a pool of up to 32 is checked with this backend's read-only inverse kinematics -- pregrasp_pose as a free_space move from the current joints, then contact_pose as a contact_approach chained from that pregrasp, trying the compiled orientation and then its 180-degree jaw flip. Candidates it calls reachable are shown first, those whose approach is within 30 degrees of straight down before the rest, each group in backend order; the cap then keeps the first max_candidates and nothing else is dropped. Each shown candidate carries ik_reachability {reachable, member, pregrasp, approach, approach_tilt_from_vertical_deg}, and the result's ik_reachability states the solver, how many pool candidates were checked and how many were reachable. It is an IK reference at planning time, not a guarantee: every motion still runs its own backend admission, and matches_move_pose_admission says whether this solver is that one. reachable null means the check was unavailable and the backend order was kept. Jaw symmetry: on this arm the same grasp turned 180 degrees about the approach axis differs only in joint6, the wrist roll (limit +/-3.14 rad). Both turns are checked, and pregrasp_pose and contact_pose are published in the reachable turn with more joint6 margin, then the one needing the smaller joint move, then the compiled one. ik_reachability.jaw_symmetry names the published turn (exact or jaw_flip), why, and each turn's joint6 margin; ik_reachability.joint_headroom gives its smallest joint-limit and joint6 margins at the pregrasp and contact solutions. Little joint6 margin leaves little wrist rotation after the grasp. Planning-time IK numbers, not a carry guarantee. Fixed texts stated once here and left out of results and effects: ik_reachability.claim_boundary is "IK reference at planning time for the compiled pregrasp (free_space from the measured joints) and approach (contact_approach from that pregrasp solution), trying the exact orientation and its 180-degree jaw flip; not a guarantee. Execution runs its own backend check, and any world action stales this."; ik_reachability.jaw_symmetry.claim_boundary is "Joint-limit margins of the backend's read-only IK solutions for the published pregrasp and contact poses at planning time; joint6 is the X5 wrist roll about the approach axis and is reported only when the measured joints prove it is the binding joint. An IK reference, not a carry guarantee: execution solves again, and lifting, carrying or rotating the wrist after the grasp moves every margin.".
replace.mark_point:
Measure up to eight visible pixels of one current RGB view as world-frame points in a single call.
Use when: one or more exact pixels — not an object identity, centre or full extent — must become world XYZ for a waypoint, clearance comparison or geometric fallback. Pass point_ids and points_uv index-aligned and of equal length, in the native top-left [x,y] coordinates of the named view, choosing pixels well inside the intended visible surface. For one pixel, pass one point_id and one points_uv entry in the same batch format.
Effect: read-only with respect to the world, but every measured pixel persists one observation-bound geometric mark under its point_id. Reusing a name already solved from another view verifies the new measurement against the stored one instead of replacing it; a disagreement beyond 25 mm fails only that entry, with error_code inconsistent_mark, and keeps the stored measurement.
Returns: a call status of solved, partial or failed, plus one marks[] entry per requested pixel in request order, each repeating its own source_index. An entry carries its own status, xyz_m in metres when it solved, the distinct views that measured that name, and its depth-support evidence — measured depth, window radius, valid, supporting and rejected sample counts, and maximum support deviation — on success and on failure alike. The call returns one composite overlay: each entry names the colour_rgb it was drawn in, and image_mapping binds a panel to a source_index rather than to its position, because inline images are evicted one block at a time. Measurement feedback states coordinate units and limitations; null residuals are unmeasured.
Does not: track a pixel through robot or camera motion, segment or identify the object, infer hidden geometry, correct a click on the wrong surface, expose simulator ground truth, or prove reachability, collision clearance, contact, retention or success. A single-view depth reading measures a visible surface, not an object centre, and eight measured pixels are not a shape.
On error: Refused: a call with more than eight entries, point_ids and points_uv of unequal lengths, a repeated or empty name, a name longer than 64 characters, a negative pixel coordinate, or a view that cannot be marked; the whole call is refused and the refusal names the field. A pixel that cannot be measured fails only its own entry and leaves the rest solved. Read that entry's error_code: aim farther inside the surface for depth_discontinuity or insufficient_depth_support, choose a different pixel for invalid_depth at the camera far plane, and resolve a disputed name from a complementary current view. A wrist camera moves with its arm, so after any motion discard old wrist pixels and query the fresh observation rather than hand-projecting the old image location.
replace.move_pose:
Submit a complete pose target through the Supervisor.
Use when: moving the public link6 controlled point to a stated position and orientation. Send one or both arms under targets; an omitted arm is not commanded. Each arm names its two choices as enums -- position_mode (hold_current, absolute, delta) and orientation_mode (hold_current, absolute_quaternion, axis_angle_delta) -- and sends that mode's fields beside them in targets.<arm>. absolute takes position_m; delta takes translation_m and position_frame; absolute_quaternion takes orientation_xyzw; axis_angle_delta takes rotation_axis, rotation_angle_deg and orientation_frame -- rotation_angle_deg is in DEGREES, and no field here takes radians. To hold one half while changing the other, set its mode to hold_current. Label the target free_space, precision or contact_approach by physical intent, not by controller name.
Effect: compiles the request once. It reserves up to 20 native actions of the task's native-action limit and stops at measured arrival. free_space always uses the global route: one SDK inverse-kinematics solve plus joint interpolation, screened for this arm's own self-collision at the endpoint and along the straight joint interpolation, and against the other arm (both arms together when one call moves both; no objects, tabletop, finger links or payload), with no trajectory planner; precision uses one bounded local Cartesian step when the complete change is within 50 mm and 15 degrees and the global route otherwise; contact_approach up to 50 mm/15 degrees is local, while a larger contact approach first reaches a pre-contact pose on the global route and locally executes only the final 40 mm/9.3 degrees. Small in-place rotations may be local. Every stage uses measured convergence and a local failure never silently falls back to global.
Returns: an immediate acknowledgement with status=submitted, action and compiled_pose; compiled_pose.targets contains the compiled requested target, not a measured arrival. The later receipt separates refusal, arrival and recoverable non-arrival, and available contact feedback includes requested versus measured motion and truthful unknown values; this backend measures no contact force. The subsequent Supervisor receipt and fresh causal observation separately report execution route, phase outcomes and measured residuals. A pre-admission error submits no action.
Does not: ask the policy to choose the global versus local route; avoid obstacles; change an exact requested orientation other than by the free_space jaw flip described below; command a gripper; move an omitted arm; infer contact, retention or task success; retry a failed local stage through another backend.
On error: Refused: an empty targets map or an arm outside left and right; an unknown field, a mode without its companion fields or a field of another mode, each naming the field; an approach_world or jaw_line_world that is not three finite numbers or is shorter than 1e-6, or a jaw line within 5 degrees of the approach axis, each naming the field; hold_current for both halves of one arm, a target equal to the measured pose, a rotation_angle_deg outside [-180, 180] or an orientation_xyzw whose norm lies outside [0.98, 1.02], each as invalid_motion_arguments without a field; a target outside the bound action workspace (workspace_bounds) unless the controlled point is already outside it and the target only reduces the violation; the episode's terminal boundary (episode_terminal). Rejected before any controller write, with no native action spent: two arms labelled with different interactions (plan_rejected, mixed_interactions); any target outside the bound action workspace, with no exception (plan_rejected, workspace_target_<axis>); a global-route solution needing a joint move above pi rad (ik_branch_jump) or a local-route one above 1 rad (local_ik_branch_jump); an IK solution that carries joint2 to joint5 out of [-pi, pi], or farther out when already outside (pitch_joint_wrap, planner_failed when no solution remains). position_mode delta without translation_m is refused at targets.<arm>.translation_m; a field belonging to another mode is refused by name. planner_failed means the bounded SDK inverse-kinematics solve admitted no joint target; plan_rejected means zero controller writes, including an inverse-kinematics branch jump (ik_branch_jump or local_ik_branch_jump) and workspace targets; not_reached means execution started but measured convergence or endpoint verification failed. Use the named phase and fresh evidence rather than repeating the same target blindly. not_reached preserves endpoint and controller evidence independently of official task termination. Read the fresh observation before proposing another action. Numerical inputs follow compute's Use when rule; send every value in this tool's declared units and frame. Every arm motion, grasp_execute stages included, stops once no joint moves 0.005 rad per native action for 3 native actions short of target, then holds its measured joints: controller_stalled with motion_progress (arms.<arm> or a stage measurement). Before submission the target gets read-only IK on its route. With empty jaws (last gripper command open), a free_space absolute orientation is also tried turned 180 degrees about the approach axis (on this arm only joint6 changes, limit +/-3.14 rad); if the requested turn fails or has under 45 degrees of joint6 margin, the reachable turn with more margin is sent. compiled_pose.targets.<arm>.jaw_symmetry names it. reach_along_request: if the target fails, the farthest solving fraction of the straight path from the current pose, and that pose. Planning-time IK only. When the target does not solve, reach_along_request also carries nearest_reachable_orientation: the smallest turn of the requested orientation (15 to 75 degrees in 15-degree steps, about axes perpendicular to the approach axis) that solves with the nominal jaw centre held, as a pose with approach_world and tilt_from_straight_down_deg, or none_within_sweep; endpoint IK only. compiled_pose.targets.<arm>.observed_clearance (also on move_to, rotate_wrist and rotate_pitch): the jaw footprint's lowest point at the target (fingers, plus the held object's localized extent when the jaws hold a named target) minus the highest surface the current depth images show beneath it or within radius_m; negative means that surface is higher; occluded surfaces are unknown; not a collision check. world_axes compiles approach_world (link6 local +X) and jaw_line_world (local +Y) into orientation_xyzw. compiled_pose.targets.<arm>.target_axes_world, on move_pose, move_to, rotate_wrist and rotate_pitch, gives the submitted orientation's world approach and jaw-line directions. Fixed texts stated once here and left out of results and effects: compiled_pose.targets.<arm>.observed_clearance.claim_boundary (move_pose, move_to, rotate_wrist and rotate_pitch) is "From the current depth images and their calibration only; points inside the measured jaws, the held object and the space above them are excluded as robot, other robot links are not; occluded surfaces and object undersides are unknown; points up to the footprint's top within radius_m count; not a collision check or a contact prediction, and the move is submitted unchanged."; last_action_effect.detail.arms.<arm>.planning_diagnostics.evidence_scope of a one-arm move is "One bounded SDK IK solve, endpoint FK checks and the SDK collision spheres sampled along the straight joint interpolation for self-collision and against the other arm at its measured joints (finger links are not in the sphere model); no scene, table, payload or task-success proof."; last_action_effect.detail.arms.<arm>.planning_diagnostics.evidence_scope of a two-arm move is "One bounded SDK IK solve, endpoint FK checks and the SDK collision spheres sampled along the straight joint interpolation for self-collision; no scene, table, payload or task-success proof."; compiled_pose.targets.<arm>.reach_along_request.claim_boundary of an unsolved target is "Read-only IK on the route move_pose takes, from the measured joints, at sampled points of the straight interpolation to the target; reachability is not proven monotone between samples, and no path, collision, payload or arrival claim."; reach_along_request.nearest_reachable_orientation.claim_boundary is "Read-only IK at each candidate endpoint on the route this move takes, from the measured joints: the requested orientation turned about axes perpendicular to its approach axis, holding the nominal jaw centre; no path, collision, payload or arrival claim, and an orientation outside the sweep may solve.".
replace.move_to:
Move selected public link6 controlled points to world-frame positions while holding each measured action-start orientation. Use when: the intended change is translation-only free-space repositioning and a position-only trajectory label is useful. Effect: world mutation; compiles through canonical move_pose with interaction=free_space, so the Runtime solves one SDK inverse-kinematics target and interpolates the joints within the command's reserved window of at most 20 native actions, stopping at measured arrival; the route is screened for this arm's own self-collision, at the endpoint and along the straight joint interpolation, and against the other arm, not against objects, the tabletop, finger links or a held payload. Returns: an immediate acknowledgement with status=submitted, action and compiled_pose; compiled_pose.targets contains the compiled requested target, not a measured arrival. The later receipt separates refusal, arrival and recoverable non-arrival; available contact feedback includes requested versus measured motion and truthful unknown values; this backend measures no contact force. The subsequent Supervisor receipt and fresh causal observation separately report execution route, phase outcomes and measured residuals. A pre-admission error submits no action.
Does not: ask the policy to select a controller implementation; rotate, command a gripper, infer contact intent, avoid obstacles, or guarantee reachability. On error: Refused: an empty targets map, an arm outside left and right or a field other than position_m; a non-finite position; a target equal to the measured position; a target outside the bound action workspace (workspace_bounds) unless the controlled point is already outside it and the target only reduces the violation, while the backend rejects any target outside it as plan_rejected (workspace_target_<axis>); the episode's terminal boundary (episode_terminal). Inspect the named failure stage and current residual, then choose a reachable intermediate or recover_pose after a genuine motion failure. Numerical inputs follow compute's Use when rule; send every value in this tool's declared units and frame. Its compiled_pose targets carry reach_along_request, as move_pose's do.
replace.observe:
Inspect current or saved public camera images without moving the world.
Use when: you need named-point overlays or a saved same-round view, including the same camera's earlier view of an object you are checking for retention. Current physical-camera RGB and calibration are already delivered automatically; use those images directly when sufficient. Calling observe does not advance or recapture the world.
Effect: read-only; step selects an immutable observation in the current round, never recaptures or rewinds the environment.
Returns: images, dimensions and actual or actual_historical_observation status; historical results name observation_step.
Does not: establish object identity, attachment or task success; historical images are not the current world.
On error: Refused: an empty or repeated views list or a view outside this tool's enum; history_point_ids naming a mark that is not solved; a step outside the current round's saved steps (invalid_arguments, naming that range); history_point_ids together with step. Choose a saved step in the current round. With step, use physical camera views only and omit history_point_ids. For a complementary retention check, inspect the same camera both at baseline and now, then segment each with its matching step. Measurement feedback states coordinate units and limitations; null residuals are unmeasured. Images are explicitly indexed when present. All current physical camera RGB and calibration are delivered automatically before decisions. Depth stays query-based; precise pixel measurements use mark_point. Omitted views selects every physical camera; request a subset only for a specific overlay or historical comparison. Public robot facts: return measured pose, controlled-frame world axes, and measured finger/command state with explicit semantics. Each returned physical camera includes native RGB dimensions, pinhole intrinsics and a world-to-camera CV transform from this exact observation; historical requests use historical calibration. Derived point-cloud panels have no pinhole calibration. Full current camera coverage is supplied automatically. Numerical joint opening alone never proves a grasp; unavailable measurements remain null or explicitly unavailable. Each calibrated camera also carries controlled_point_pixels and jaw_center_pixels per arm: the native OpenCV pixel [x, y], inside_image, in_front_of_camera and depth_m, computed from that camera's calibration and the measured pose of the same observation (automatic current delivery carries the same fields). The controlled point is the link6 wrist flange, which sits behind the arm's own wrist camera, so its wrist pixel is null. The jaw contact centre is the nominal pad contact centre 0.1501 m ahead of link6 along the approach axis; in the arm's own wrist camera it projects near the horizontal centre, below the image centre, not at it. Centring an object in a wrist view therefore does not put it between the jaws; compare the object with jaw_center_pixels instead. It is nominal source geometry, not a measured contact or grasp. Delivered copies leave out what they would only repeat. In public_robot_facts a camera entry omits native_pixel_to_image_offset_xy when it is [0, 0] and image_view when it is that camera's own name; end effectors omit orientation_order and controlled_frame, because every pose is [x, y, z, qx, qy, qz, qw] of the controlled point the embodiment card names. In last_action_effect.detail an arm that was not targeted lists only its non-null fields, and its inactive_arm_drift only above 0.1 mm or 0.01 deg. A claim_boundary, evidence_scope or note whose fixed text a tool's description states is left out of that tool's results and effects. An arm's gripper.feedback.arrival_check omits tolerance_normalized when it equals controller_feedback.gripper_tolerance_normalized.
replace.recover_pose: Move selected arms to a named robot-only recovery configuration while preserving all gripper commands. Use when: a planner/execution failure or poor configuration makes ordinary waypoint correction inappropriate; choose previous to return to the joint configuration measured when that arm's most recent admitted pose action started, whether or not it arrived, and choose home for a deliberate return to the RoboDojo episode reset joints. Prefer one-arm recovery unless both arms genuinely require synchronized retreat. Effect: world mutation through the canonical recovery boundary; the stored joints are reached by joint interpolation with no planner, in a joint order screened for this arm's own self-collision and against the other arm (no objects, tabletop, finger links or held payload), omitted arms receive no drive target, and a recovery does not replace the saved previous configuration. Returns: submitted public strategies and recovery mapping immediately; the next receipt and fresh observation report actual execution, residuals, preservation and drift. The later receipt separates refusal, arrival and recoverable non-arrival; available contact feedback includes requested versus measured motion and truthful unknown values; this backend measures no contact force. Does not: reset the episode, restore moved objects or evaluator state, release a gripper, reverse an old trajectory, undo physics, act as an emergency stop, model scene or payload collisions, or guarantee escape from contact. On error: Refused: an empty targets map, an arm outside left and right or a strategy other than previous and home; the episode's terminal boundary (episode_terminal). Rejected before any controller write, as plan_rejected: stored or measured joints that are missing or non-finite (recovery_state_unavailable). Inspect each arm result and scene state, retry one arm at a time or use the other strategy only when physically sensible; if both recovery routes are exhausted or unsafe, finish_episode names the accepted outcomes. On this backend each arm stops at arrival or on the move_pose stall rule, and arms.<arm>.recovery_progress gives outcome (arrived, stalled or still_moving_at_window_end) with joint_distance_start_rad and joint_distance_end_rad. home first lifts link6 up to 0.10 m straight up, orientation held, then unwinds the joints in an order the SDK collision spheres keep clear of the arm itself and of the other arm, or refuses with recovery_self_collision_path or recovery_inter_arm_collision_path, before moving or at the step that would meet the other arm. Joints move about 0.2 rad per native action, so a wound arm can need a second call.
replace.report_issue:
Persist one concise policy-visible interface, tool or evidence defect. Use when: a concrete inconsistency—such as a malformed result, stale observation binding, contradictory camera evidence or missing capability—prevents reliable action; normal task difficulty is not itself an interface issue. Effect: read-only with respect to the robot world and appends one diagnostic record without ending the episode. Returns: an acknowledgement after the diagnostic record is persisted; the Native acknowledgement may contain no additional decision fields.
Does not: repair the defect, move the robot, change task state, consume a robot decision, establish official failure or finish the policy session. On error: Refused: any field other than message, or a message that is empty or only whitespace (invalid_arguments). Reduce the message to one reproducible symptom and retry once; continue only if the remaining evidence is safe and internally consistent.
replace.rotate_pitch:
Tilt the current approach axis while holding position.
Use when: rotating selected public link6 controlled points about each action-start local +Y jaw-separation axis while holding link6 position, usually to change the approach direction.
Effect: compiles to an exact pose. Rotations within 15 degrees use one bounded local Cartesian inverse-kinematics step; larger rotations use the global inverse-kinematics plus joint-interpolation route.
Returns: an immediate acknowledgement with status=submitted, action and compiled_pose; compiled_pose.targets contains the compiled requested target, not a measured arrival. The subsequent Supervisor receipt and fresh causal observation separately report execution route, phase outcomes and measured residuals. A pre-admission error submits no action.
Does not: expose a literal robot joint, imply that positive pitch is always world-down, translate by request, infer surface alignment, command a gripper or maintain contact force.
On error: Refused: an empty targets map or an arm outside left and right; an angle outside [-180, 180] degrees or not a finite number; an angle of 0; a target outside the bound action workspace (workspace_bounds), which includes any rotation while the controlled point is already outside it; the episode's terminal boundary (episode_terminal). Inspect realized axes and residuals, then correct sign/magnitude or use move_pose when position must co-vary. A failed local rotation is not retried through global planning. Numerical inputs follow compute's Use when rule; send every value in this tool's declared units and frame. Its compiled_pose targets carry reach_along_request, as move_pose's do.
replace.rotate_wrist:
Rotate the jaw line around the current approach axis while holding position.
Use when: rotating selected public link6 controlled points about each action-start local +X approach axis while holding link6 position, usually to align the jaw-closing line.
Effect: compiles to an exact pose. Rotations within 15 degrees use one bounded local Cartesian inverse-kinematics step; larger rotations use the global inverse-kinematics plus joint-interpolation route.
Returns: an immediate acknowledgement with status=submitted, action and compiled_pose; compiled_pose.targets contains the compiled requested target, not a measured arrival. The subsequent Supervisor receipt and fresh causal observation separately report execution route, phase outcomes and measured residuals. A pre-admission error submits no action.
Does not: expose a literal wrist joint, translate by request, infer object alignment, command a gripper, maintain contact force or change the signed requested angle.
On error: Refused: an empty targets map or an arm outside left and right; an angle outside [-180, 180] degrees or not a finite number; an angle of 0; a target outside the bound action workspace (workspace_bounds), which includes any rotation while the controlled point is already outside it; the episode's terminal boundary (episode_terminal). Inspect the current link6 axes and residual; correct sign/magnitude or use move_pose when position must co-vary. A failed local rotation is not retried through global planning. Numerical inputs follow compute's Use when rule; send every value in this tool's declared units and frame. Its compiled_pose targets carry reach_along_request, as move_pose's do.
replace.set_gripper:
Set one or both grippers to a named directive in a single call.
Use when: you are opening to release or approach, or closing to grasp, and you already know which directive each gripper should hold. On a two-armed embodiment this is how the two are coordinated: naming both in one call is the only way to state that they change together. Near miss: this is not grasp_execute. If you have chosen a current grasp candidate and accept the committed sequence without intermediate decisions, call that instead -- it approaches, closes and measures as one committed sequence, and a bare close here does none of that. Use this standalone command when a separate decision after pose execution is needed.
Effect: submits one gripper directive per named gripper through the Supervisor; an accepted command consumes one robot decision, and a refusal that executed no native actions and changed nothing consumes none. **An omitted gripper holds its current directive; it is not re-sent and not re-actuated.** The end-effector pose target is held unchanged. Measured state may still move under contact, and that is evidence rather than a fault.
Returns: a submitted acknowledgement, then a measured receipt and a fresh observation on the next turn. When closing, an intent block echoes the target_ref you supplied and labels it agent_annotation_only.
Does not: prove anything was grasped, held, released or moved; report jaw separation; verify what the jaws closed on; or make target_ref evidence -- it is your annotation of what you believe you are closing on, never a measurement. A closed jaw is not a grasp.
On error: Refused: an empty targets map or an arm outside left and right, or a directive other than open and close; a target_ref that is blank or not a string (invalid_arguments, naming target_ref); the episode's terminal boundary (episode_terminal). A schema refusal is invalid_arguments naming the field; an invalid_motion_arguments refusal names none -- re-read this schema rather than resubmitting the same shape. invalid_arguments naming target_ref means a blank string was sent; send a non-empty reference or omit it entirely. Timing: one native action is 10 physics steps of 4 ms (25 Hz, 40 ms per native action), so one command's 20 native actions last at most 0.8 s. Under the SDK drive limiter the jaws travel at most about 0.16 of the opening per native action: a free-air close from fully open reaches the closed floor (normalized opening about 0.185) in about 6 native actions (0.24 s), and a free-air open from closed takes about 8 (0.32 s). A command ends as soon as every named gripper is within 0.03 of its effective target, or has stopped short of it: three consecutive native actions that each moved less than 0.005 of the normalized opening. A close that stops on an object therefore ends 3 native actions (0.12 s) after the jaws stop, and reports not_reached with failure_code gripper_stalled_before_target and, for each named arm, arms.<arm>.gripper_outcome: state, commanded_opening_normalized, effective_target_opening_normalized, measured_opening_normalized (both fingers' mean), sdk_limited_drive_target_normalized (0.2 below the first finger's reading while the jaws are held apart), measured_finger_displacements_m, finger_lateral_offset_m, primary_finger_limit_holds_close (true when the close stopped with the second finger at that held target), ticks_used, ticks_budget and seconds_used. That is the expected result of closing on an object, not a controller fault. gripper_not_reached with state moving_at_budget means a jaw was still moving when the 20 native actions ran out. A stalled close is consistent with a grasp but does not prove one, and the normalized opening is not a calibrated jaw width: lift and observe to check retention. Fixed texts stated once here and left out of results and effects: the action effect's gripper_outcome.claim_boundary is "stalled_before_target means the jaws stopped short of the commanded opening; it is consistent with an object between the fingers and is not proof of a grasp".
replace.vision_ground: Retrieve up to three inspectable text-grounded target proposals from one selected current RGB-D camera. Use when: task language names an object or part and the scene-level search space should be reduced before the policy makes its own identity decision; begin with the widest useful view, then choose head or a useful wrist to resolve a concrete ambiguity. Treat the returned set as recall-oriented proposals: top rank and backend score are within-call ordering signals, not an oracle. Effect: read-only and creates one separate observation-bound target_ref per candidate. Returns: ranked candidates, source camera, bounding boxes, mask-area/depth summaries and numbered overlay; compare all plausible candidates against visible colour, shape, scale, location and surrounding context before selecting one. Does not: choose the correct candidate, guarantee that rank 0 is foreground, combine cameras, expose object ground truth, calibrate scores across calls, or prove absence when current coverage misses the target. On error: Refused: max_candidates outside 1 to 3, before any request is sent; text that is empty after trimming or longer than 120 characters; a camera outside this tool's enum; no grounding service (grounding_unavailable); a request the grounding service rejects (invalid_arguments, with the service's detail). Reject a candidate whose overlay or mask is dominated by table, robot, background or an implausibly large region even when its score is highest; inspect another returned proposal, rephrase a short visible description, switch current camera, or use vision_segment only after you can point safely inside the intended instance. Selection check: compare the requested task referent with every candidate crop and the original view; rank 0 and a high score do not authenticate identity. Separate an instance hypothesis from an observed property. Failed grasping is not evidence that the intended object is static or that a different object is the target. Revise a mistaken association when the visible evidence contradicts it. Boundary and mask/depth diagnostics describe observability, not semantic truth. Localization also carries a single-view support estimate: support_z_m is the height of the surface the target stands on, fitted to depth pixels just outside its mask and evaluated under it; height_above_support_m is the visible top's height above that surface; mid_height_z_m is the midpoint between them; support_point_count counts the pixels that support the fit, and the three heights are null when no support is visible. center_xyz_m is a visible-surface median, so from an oblique or overhead camera it sits near the top; for a parallel-jaw side grasp, use mid_height_z_m as the height reference instead. The estimate is not ground truth: a neighbouring object, a container wall or a hidden base can bias it.
replace.vision_segment:
Propose a small mask set from several independent points on one public image.
Use when: comparing plausible regions around the intended object; give 1–8 source-pixel points, usually 3–5 separated interior points. Every point is queried independently, not jointly as one mask prompt, and every point comes back with its own answer.
Effect: world-read-only; binds one current or saved same-round RGB-D view, reuses its image encoding, keeps each point's own SAM alternatives and records immutable masks and per-point query outcomes.
Returns: candidates[] and queries[], one query entry per input point in input order. max_candidates is a PER-POINT budget (default 3, maximum 3): every point's leading mask is admitted before any point's second, so a point that produced a usable mask always keeps one. Each candidate carries its T-index, delivery position, target_ref, score, source queries, geometry and depth/normalization limitations; a mask several points share costs one artifact and is listed under each of them. At most 12 distinct masks and 5 enlarged crops are delivered, and each point reports omitted_over_point_limit and omitted_over_call_cap separately from status no_candidate, which means no mask at that pixel rather than a spent budget. Inspect the proposals and select the intended semantic region.
Does not: require position 0 to be the intended object, prove identity, add sensor resolution by enlargement, mutate the world or grant motion permission. Score orders proposals within one point only; scores from different points are not evidence of which point is right. A point on background, boundary or shadow can return the table, robot or a neighbour. Historical pixels never become current geometry after motion.
On error: Refused: no point or more than eight; a point outside the source image, which refuses the whole call; max_candidates outside 1 to 3; a camera outside this tool's enum; a step outside the current round's saved steps (invalid_arguments, naming that range); a request the segmentation service rejects (invalid_arguments, with the service's detail). Correct the named input or source. If no candidate matches the intended region, choose better interior points or another public view; a failed or empty point preserves every other point's results. A disconnected mask keeps the prompted component and reports what was removed. Localization also carries a single-view support estimate: support_z_m is the height of the surface the target stands on, fitted to depth pixels just outside its mask and evaluated under it; height_above_support_m is the visible top's height above that surface; mid_height_z_m is the midpoint between them; support_point_count counts the pixels that support the fit, and the three heights are null when no support is visible. center_xyz_m is a visible-surface median, so from an oblique or overhead camera it sits near the top; for a parallel-jaw side grasp, use mid_height_z_m as the height reference instead. The estimate is not ground truth: a neighbouring object, a container wall or a hidden base can bias it. Fixed texts stated once here and left out of results and effects: the result's claim_boundary is "independent point-prompt proposals with a per-point mask budget; one point never consumes another point's masks, an empty point means no mask at that pixel rather than an exhausted budget, and omitted_over_* counts every mask withheld; inspect the proposals and choose semantic identity; crops add no sensor detail".
replace.wait_ticks:
Hold every current command and let simulated time pass.
Use when: the scene has to change without a robot command -- a scripted demonstration or task animation is running, a released object is still settling, or the task says to wait. It is not a correction: a pose residual needs move_pose, a stalled jaw needs set_gripper.
Effect: world mutation by elapsed time only. Every applied drive target and gripper directive is held unchanged; nothing is planned, re-ramped or re-limited. ticks control ticks elapse, one tick being 10 physics steps (40 ms of simulated time), at most 20 per call. One call is one robot decision.
Returns: status=submitted immediately. The next receipt reports wait.ticks_used, wait.physics_steps and each arm's inactive_arm_drift while held; the fresh observation shows what changed.
Does not: move toward any target, open or close a gripper, restore a drifted pose, or establish that the scene changed or that a demonstration finished.
On error: Refused: any field other than ticks, or ticks that is not an integer from 1 to 20 (invalid_arguments, naming the ticks bound); the episode's terminal boundary (episode_terminal). For more time call wait_ticks again; act once a fresh observation shows the scene you need. On this backend one tick is one native action, the unit the task's native-action limit counts. A scripted demonstrator or support arm in the scene advances only while native actions are consumed, so wait_ticks is how it runs without moving the robot. Fixed texts stated once here and left out of results and effects: last_action_effect.detail.wait.claim_boundary is "time passed with commands held; drift, settling, slip or scripted scene motion are measured evidence in the fresh observation, not effects of this action".
